- [5.3] 'given up animal strength to manipulate subtle instruments, like hammers, spears, and—later—pens and pencils': the infinitive of purpose and 'like' for examples are both fine.
- [6.1] 'default circuit—essentially, the areas of the brain responsible for …': the apposition of a singular term with a plural explanation is acceptable.
- [7.3] 'Cultivating drawing talent can become an essential tool to improve …': loose but grammatical.
- [8.1] 'Rather than think …, we should consider it as a tool …—one that just so happens to double as an art form': the bare infinitive after 'rather than' is parallel with 'should consider'. 'Consider sth as sth' is accepted (Cambridge lists 'consider sb/sth (as) sth'). 'Just so happens to' is a standard idiom.
- [8.2] 'have been shown to positively affect your memory …, so complain loudly …': the split infinitive is fine, and the shift to 'your' plus an imperative is deliberate direct address.

On the already-decided paragraph break before 'There's also evidence…': the print shows a short last line before it and the line starts flush left. I have no new reason to change that decision.

notes.logic:
I compared the whole passage word for word with both page images (p7 and p8). I found six differences from the printed page. Four look like deliberately planted errors that the paper does not have: have/has, Siting/Sitting, women/woman and an/a. The other two are 'disappear' instead of 'appear', which reverses the logic, and a lost paragraph break before 'The problem comes when…'. The printed passage has 6 paragraphs; the current text has 5.

These sentences got the closest look under the word-choice, logic and fact lens, and I kept all of them:
(1) 'most of their lives will be spent making short journeys': 'their' refers to the cars, and that reading is fine.
(2) 'parking sensors, sound systems, and navigation apps': the serial comma is fine.
(3) 'This seems to be one of the few areas where the benefit of sharing personal information comes straight back to the sharer: because…': the logic and punctuation are fine.
(4) 'When a lucky few have access to the knowledge… But when everyone has perfect information, traffic jams simply spread onto the side roads': this is consistent once 'appear' is restored.
(5) 'do not miraculously produce a situation in which everyone does better than before, but one in which almost everyone does rather worse': the 'not… but' structure is correct.
(6) 'though even that much is never guaranteed': this is idiomatic.
(7) 'the taxi company Uber… a woman pushing her bicycle across a wide road in Arizona… the first recorded death involving a car which was supposed to be fully autonomous': this matches the facts of the March 2018 Tempe crash, the first pedestrian killed by a self-driving test car. Calling Uber a 'taxi company' is loose but acceptable journalistic usage.
(8) 'Experts have said that it suggests a “catastrophic failure” of technology': this is fine.
(9) 'characterises' and 'realised': British spelling, so I kept them.

The Chinese glosses (堵塞) and (令人陶醉的) match the printed page.
